text:
sasha: quick sync — we need to finalize a low-cardinality span naming + a stable set of semantic attrs for LLM requests. goal: make signal easy to query in traces and pipelines without exploding cardinality or losing useful context.

jordan: +1. 2 proposals: (A) verb-only span names like `llm.request` / `llm.kv_lookup` + attributes for model/action/details, or (B) more descriptive names `llm.generate.modelname` etc. A avoids cardinality but hurts quick-ops filtering by model.

pat: i'm leaning A. Put mutable bits (model, variant, quant) in attributes: `service.name=redwood-inference`, `span.name=llm.request` and `llm.action=generate|embed|score|kv_lookup`.

mike: agree with pat. suggest standardized attr keys: `llm.model`, `llm.model_version`, `llm.model_size`, `llm.quantization`, `llm.action`, `llm.batch_size`, `llm.input_tokens`, `llm.output_tokens`, `llm.total_tokens`, `llm.kv_cache_hits`, `llm.kv_cache_lookups`, `llm.cache_hit_rate`, `llm.routing_policy`, `llm.quota_bucket`. keep them short and dot-delimited.

jordan: can we also include `llm.run_id` or `llm.request_id`? useful to join logs/traces. but watch PII. run_id OK. also suggest `llm.fallback=true` for routed fallback cases.

sasha: agreed on run_id. also we need to decide which attrs are indexed/exported to our analytics pipeline vs kept only in trace payload (to save storage). proposal: index `llm.model`, `llm.action`, `llm.total_tokens`, `llm.cache_hit_rate`, `llm.routing_policy`, `llm.fallback` for first 30d full-resolution. keep `llm.input_tokens`/`llm.output_tokens` in trace but rollup metrics derived into metrics store.

pat: for retention/exporters: telemetry-bot, can we set rule: traces with `llm.total_tokens>10000` and `llm.fallback=true` should be sampled at higher rate and forwarded to long-term retention for debugging?

telemetry-bot: noted. suggested sampling rules: default 1% retention for llm.request spans, 10% for `llm.total_tokens>2000`, 100% for `llm.fallback=true` or `llm.error=true`. export keys: `llm.model`, `llm.action`, `llm.total_tokens` always included in OTEL resource attributes exported.

mike: about span name shape — i still want a tiny hint for op type so top-level UI can pick up without scanning attributes. compromise: use `llm.op` pattern like `llm.op:generate` as span.name or `llm.request` with `llm.action`. which is less confusing?

pat: prefer `llm.request` and rely on `llm.action`. UI can index action. avoids sprawl.

jordan: one more: kv cache attributes — prefer `llm.kv_cache_hits` (int) and `llm.kv_cache_lookups` (int) rather than boolean; compute hit rate downstream. prevents loss of info for analysis. also include `llm.kv_prefix` as low-cardinality tag when customers opt-in.

sasha: excellent. draft example span payload (pseudo):
```json
{
  "service.name": "redwood-inference",
  "span.name": "llm.request",
  "llm.action": "generate",
  "llm.model": "open-llama-3b",
  "llm.model_version": "v1.2",
  "llm.quantization": "q4_0",
  "llm.batch_size": "1",
  "llm.input_tokens": "86",
  "llm.output_tokens": "210",
  "llm.total_tokens": "296",
  "llm.kv_cache_hits": "3",
  "llm.kv_cache_lookups": "5",
  "llm.routing_policy": "latency-priority",
  "llm.quota_bucket": "free-tier",
  "llm.fallback": "false",
  "llm.run_id": "run_2024-11-06_42"
}
```

mike: looks good. small nit: ensure numeric attrs are numeric in OTEL (not strings) — we should document types for each key.

sasha: action items: (1) mike to write attr key + type table and sample OTEL instrumentation patch (PR target eng-runtime repo), (2) telemetry team to add sampling/export rules and mapping to metrics (tokens per req, cache_hit_rate), (3) product/console to confirm which attrs surface in the dashboard and quick filters. will sync friday.

pat: :thumbsup:

jordan: :eyes:

sasha: thanks all — i'll post RFC draft in #eng-platform later today and link to this thread.
